symptom: Explicit terminal-conversion branch dispatch was tested with both e30-base and mid-anchor-parent base models, routing cracked-star-jar 210-240s to the terminal-window w10 model. The e30-base branch passed e30 no-regression and online action-distribution delta but still recorded 0.0/0.0/0.0 win rate at 300s and failed parent preservation with 9 blockers. The parent-base branch preserved 60/180s behavior but still recorded 0.0/0.0/0.0 at 300s and dropped cracked-star-jar 300s average survival by 0.4779s relative to parent.
root_cause: The terminal-window w10 model does not provide enough action separation or closed-loop win conversion when used as a narrow 210-240s branch. Restricting dispatch removes global action-distribution drift, but it also leaves the underlying 300s long-run route recovery gap unresolved and slightly hurts the target map under the stronger parent base.
fix: Reject both explicit branch probes as policy evidence. Do not continue adjusting only dispatch seconds for the same terminal model. The next repair should train a true terminal-conversion branch or collect successful terminal-state trajectories with pressure/low-health context, then rerun e30 and parent no-regression, online action-distribution delta, 60/180/300s high-pressure, failure analysis, and repair gate.
